correctness.rationale: For independent uniform spanning trees of K_{a,b}, the inclusion projection H_{(i,j),(k,l)}=delta_{ik}/b+delta_{jl}/a-1/(ab), with p=(a+b-1)/(ab), gives P(e,f both in one tree)=p^2-H_{ef}^2 for distinct edges. Squaring the one-tree joint probabilities for the two independent trees and summing all three edge-pair geometries yields E X=(n-1)^2/(ab) and Var X=(a-1)(b-1)(n^2-5n+7)/(a^2b^2). Log differentiation of h_n(x) gives the sign factor (n-2x)[2n-2-x(n-x)] and reduces the fixed-n maximum to x=2,3; their exact difference is -(n-5)(n^2-12n+23)/[36(n-2)^2(n-3)^2], positive n=6..9, negative n>=10; n4,5 only x2. Stars have zero variance. Independently enumerated all spanning trees for K2,2, K2,3 and K3,3 (4,12,81 trees); exact overlap variances 3/16, 7/18, 52/81 match. This finite check corroborates the analytic all-n argument. Fixed a and b->infinity gives linear variance (a-1)b/a^2, balanced variance ->4.

value.rationale: The fluctuations of agreement between two independent network skeletons form a natural graph statistic, distinct from average overlap. An exact full-family variance and a sharp discrete optimizer change at ten vertices provide a reusable extremal benchmark and explain why thin-side variance grows with graph order whereas balanced-side variance stays bounded; not merely an isolated value or routine renaming.
